PullRequest.Title: Add beforeText condition to auto-closing pairs
PullRequest.Body:

Related to #583

## Summary

Adds an optional `beforeText` regular expression to auto-closing pairs. Languages can use it to insert the closing string only when the current-line text before the cursor, including the just-typed opening string, matches the configured expression.

## Manual Verification

Use the following language configuration:

```
"autoClosingPairs": [
    {
      "beforeText": "^\\s*begin",
      "open": "begin ",
      "close": "end"
    }
  ]
```

- [x] Type `begin ` at the start of a line and verify that `end` is inserted.
- [x] Type `begin ` after a whitespace and verify that `end` is inserted.
- [x] Type `prefixbegin ` and verify that `end` is not inserted.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path from every non-composition typing event through typeWithInterceptors/getAutoClosingPairClose/_findAutoClosingPairOpen is direct, and the new range read is visibly evaluated before shouldAutoCloseBefore can discover that beforeText is undefined. The exact delay depends on line length and cursor count, but the added synchronous work and allocation are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous piece-tree range lookups plus newly allocated prefix strings on the editor input path
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each typed opening delimiter, cost grows with the sum of the cursor columns for every matching candidate; multi-cursor edits on long/minified lines allocate and scan a full prefix per cursor before the edit can proceed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased keystroke latency and avoidable allocation/GC pressure, with visible input jank on long lines or many cursors.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The candidate check read only the short span needed to compare the configured opening string. Existing language configurations without beforeText did not copy the text from column 1 to every cursor during candidate selection.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After an opening candidate matches, the changed line synchronously copies the entire line prefix for every cursor and passes it to shouldAutoCloseBefore; this happens even though that method immediately returns true for the overwhelmingly common beforeText === undefined case.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 348 adds model.getValueInRange(new Range(position.lineNumber, 1, ..., position.column)) inside the candidate/cursor loop without checking candidate.beforeText, introducing a whole-prefix read for all matching auto-closing pairs.
Findings.Title: Skip prefix extraction for unconditional auto-closing pairs
Findings.Impact: Typing common delimiters such as quotes, braces, and parentheses now performs an extra O(cursor-column) model read/allocation per cursor even for existing pairs that do not use the new option. Long generated/minified lines and multi-cursor typing can therefore stall the synchronous input handler and add GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: _findAutoClosingPairOpen is called directly by the normal typing interceptor. The added getValueInRange spans column 1 through position.column and runs inside both the candidate and positions loops. StandardAutoClosingPairConditional.shouldAutoCloseBefore immediately returns true when beforeText is absent, proving the extracted prefix is unused for legacy pairs. TextModel.getValueInRange delegates to the piece-tree and returns a newly constructed string; later processing already reads the line again with getLineContent.
Findings.Recommendation: Guard the extraction and predicate with candidate.beforeText (or make shouldAutoCloseBefore accept a lazily supplied prefix), so the full prefix is read only for pairs that actually configure this condition; preserve lastIndex reset and matching semantics for configured regexes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing an auto-closing opening delimiter in the editor, including multi-cursor typing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The keyboard/composition interceptor synchronously calls AutoClosingOpenCharTypeOperation.getAutoClosingPairClose and _findAutoClosingPairOpen before an edit result can be returned. The newly added whole-prefix read and optional regex test are therefore directly on the keystroke critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous piece-tree getValueInRange from line start to the cursor, producing a prefix string
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-prefix read per cursor for each candidate whose opening text matches and is still eligible; normally one per cursor for common single-character pairs, potentially more for overlapping multi-character pairs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Candidate matching read only a short range the size of the opening token; no whole-prefix extraction occurred at this stage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the typed edit is produced, adding input latency and allocation/GC pressure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective multiplicity is the number of cursors times the matching candidates that remain longer than the current result; in common configurations this is usually one matching pair per cursor. The bytes copied scale with each cursor's column, so long/minified lines and multi-cursor edits dominate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All candidates and cursors are evaluated serially on the editor thread; there is no limiter, deferral, or parallelism. Separate keyboard events are naturally sequenced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Auto-closing-pair maps and compiled RegExp objects are retained in the language configuration and reused. There is no cache for line prefixes; every matching typing event performs fresh model reads and allocations, regardless of warm configuration state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added range starts at column 1 inside both loops, argument evaluation occurs even when beforeText is undefined, and TextModel delegates synchronously to the piece-tree before returning a string.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact delay varies with line length, piece-tree fragmentation, cursor count, and runtime GC. The regression is most visible on long generated/minified lines or many cursors; prevalence of those cases is uncertain, which supports medium rather than high severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: all legacy pairs pay the new whole-prefix cost even though their predicate immediately returns true. Guarding the read on candidate.beforeText preserves the feature while removing the broad hot-path tax.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load and register a declarative language-configuration file containing auto-closing pairs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the configuration has been loaded and parsed by the extension contribution machinery, LanguageConfigurationFileHandler validates each pair and now compiles beforeText only when present, then registers the resulting configuration. This is activation/configuration work rather than the typing critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work is linear in the configured auto-closing-pair count and total regex source length; typical language configurations contain a small fixed list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation and registration are synchronous and serial for one language configuration; language activations may occur independently but this code does not create a concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The RegExp is compiled once during configuration extraction and retained with the registered language configuration. Warm typing reuses it; there is no repeated compilation per keystroke.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _extractValidAutoClosingPairs conditionally calls _parseRegex once per pair and stores the result; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call occurs in the changed handler after it receives the already-loaded object.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension configurations can theoretically be large, but realistic pair counts and patterns are small and registration frequency is low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added compilation is conditional, bounded by configuration size, and amortized over the configuration lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: An extension calls languages.setLanguageConfiguration with beforeText RegExp metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension-host serialization and the single $setLanguageConfiguration RPC must complete for registration to reach the main thread, where regexes are revived and the language configuration is registered. This is configuration-registration latency and is off the per-keystroke path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ext-host to main-thread $setLanguageConfiguration carrying the complete serialized configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per setLanguageConfiguration call, independent of pair count; beforeText adds two small fields only for configured pairs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single RPC transported all language-configuration data and auto-closing pairs; the diff only enriches individual pair DTOs with optional regex source and flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration waits for the existing send/revival path, but no new round trip or fan-out is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Serialization/revival scales linearly with the number of auto-closing pairs and total regex source/flags bytes after one configuration-level grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One existing RPC carries the entire serialized language configuration; the diff does not add per-pair RPCs or extra concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The revived RegExp objects are retained by the language configuration registration and reused until disposal/replacement. There is no cold retry or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: serialization maps pairs locally, one existing proxy call sends the aggregate DTO, and main-thread revival maps it once before registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Third-party extensions can provide unusually many or large patterns, but the transport remains one grouped registration and no evidence establishes realistic harmful payload sizes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: optional metadata modestly increases one existing registration payload and one-time allocations without changing boundary cardinality or moving IPC onto typing.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all ten changed files and traced typing, declarative configuration, and extension-registration scenarios. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity hot-path regression for unconditional full-prefix extraction; no additional boundary, cache, concurrency, lifecycle, or registration regression met the reporting threshold.
